back: A series with many zero periods and occasional demands of varying size. Typical for spare parts and slow-moving items.
It smooths demand size z and interval p with SES, updating only in periods with demand. Forecast is z / p per period.
Multiply Croston's forecast by (1 - alpha/2) to remove its positive bias.
It smooths the probability of demand in every period, so the forecast decays when an item stops selling. Forecast = probability times size.

front: What are ADI and CV squared?
back: ADI: average periods between demands. CV squared: squared variation of non-zero sizes. Cut-offs 1.32 and 0.49 classify demand.

front: Why is MAE misleading for intermittent demand?
back: The median is zero, so a forecast of zero gets the lowest MAE. Use scaled errors, or quantiles for inventory.
